findings.evidence: The only fetched historical state is the current `refs/pull/*/head` (lines 160–167); `createdAt` is fetched at line 188 but never bounds replay, while lines 245–252 explicitly convert commits into purported push epochs and lines 267–270 unconditionally label the next epoch a push resolution.
findings.fix: Base epochs on actual recorded PR-head transitions and verify the next head is mergeable before ending an episode; if those transitions are unavailable historically, remove the claimed baseline rather than inferring them from commit dates.
findings.issue: `pr_heads` treats every surviving commit timestamp as a time that commit was the published PR head; local commits may be pushed together, timestamps can predate PR creation, and old force-pushed heads are absent. Lines 267–270 then count every following commit as a conflict-resolving push even when its head remains conflicting, producing invented episodes and durations.

findings.evidence: `episodes()` iterates `open_prs()` at line 456, and its own lines 450–451 confirm merged/closed PR histories are intentionally excluded.
findings.fix: Query all PRs relevant to the requested time window and read their marker comments, classifying live state separately from PR lifecycle.
findings.issue: `report` reads markers only from currently open PRs, so resolved episodes vanish as soon as their PR merges or closes; the reported median and tail cannot measure conflict-to-resolution over a week as claimed.

summary: The historical replay does not reconstruct PR-head history, and the ongoing report discards completed PRs, so both advertised conflict-latency measurements are semantically invalid.
